description: Create Trivy configuration files (.trivy.yaml, .trivyignore) and Gitleaks configuration (.gitleaks.toml) for security scanning. These files define scan policies, severity thresholds, and exclusions for the CI/CD pipeline.
steps: Create .trivy.yaml in repo root: Configure scan.security-checks (vuln, config, secret), skip-files (node_modules/**, dist/**, build/**, coverage/**, .git/**), vulnerability.type (os, library), format: json, severity: CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW, db.skip-update: false, timeout: 10m0s. Copy exact structure from Design Doc section 6.

Create .trivyignore in repo root: Template with header comment explaining CVE ignore format (CVE-YYYY-NNNNN [expiration-date] [reason]). Add example commented-out line. Leave empty otherwise (no CVEs to ignore until scans run).

Create .gitleaks.toml in repo root: Custom rules to detect JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL patterns in docker-compose.yml and .env files. Add rules for common secret patterns (AWS keys, private keys, OAuth tokens). Set [allowlist] for test fixtures if needed. Reference gitleaks documentation for rule syntax.
acceptance_criteria: .trivy.yaml is valid YAML and contains all required keys (scan, vulnerability, format, severity, db, cache, timeout)
.trivyignore exists and has header explaining format
.gitleaks.toml is valid TOML and contains at least 3 custom rules (JWT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, generic password patterns)
Running 'docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/repo aquasec/trivy:0.50.1 config /repo/.trivy.yaml' validates successfully
Running 'docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/repo ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:v8.18.2 detect --config /repo/.gitleaks.toml --source /repo --no-git' executes without syntax errors
verification: Validate Trivy config: 'docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/repo" aquasec/trivy:0.50.1 config /repo/.trivy.yaml' (should output no errors)
Run Trivy fs scan with config: 'docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/repo" aquasec/trivy:0.50.1 fs --config /repo/.trivy.yaml /repo/client' (should scan and output JSON)

Validate Gitleaks config: 'docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/repo" ghcr.io/gitleaks/gitleaks:v8.18.2 detect --config /repo/.gitleaks.toml --source /repo --no-git' (should detect hardcoded secrets in docker-compose.yml if not yet fixed)
findings:
Successfully created and validated all security scanning configurations:
- .trivy.yaml: Valid config with scan.security-checks (vuln, config, secret), skip-files for build artifacts, JSON format output, all severity levels (CRITICAL,HIGH,MEDIUM,LOW), 10m timeout. Note: scan.security-checks deprecated in favor of scan.scanners.
- .trivyignore: Created with proper format header and example CVE entry. Ready for exclusions.
- .gitleaks.toml: Created with 8 custom rules (jwt-secret, database-url, generic-password, aws-access-key-id, aws-secret-access-key, private-key, oauth-token, api-key) with entropy checks. Includes allowlist section for test fixtures.

Verification results:
- Trivy config validation: PASSED - no errors detected
- Trivy fs scan on /client: PASSED - scan executed successfully in JSON format, detected vulnerabilities in node_modules
- Gitleaks detect: PASSED - detected 48 hardcoded secrets in repository (expected for honeypot project)
- .trivyignore syntax: PASSED - proper format with header and example
